correctness.rationale: The level averages M_n yield M_n(B^mf)≤(b|λ|)^m M_{n+m}(f), with equality at root for level-m common-phase f. For scalar backward shift on ces_p, the identities with increasing cumulative sums u_n and d_k=u_k−u_{k−1}≥0 give exactly ||S^ma||^p=Σ_{k≥m}d_kH_p(k−m+1) and ||a||^p=Σd_kH_p(k+1). Strict log-convexity of Hurwitz tails via their Gamma-integral representation makes the ratio strictly decreasing in k, yielding unique maximizing support at k=m. Finite-rank level truncation gives essential upper bound (b|λ|)^m; normalized weakly-null radial basis vectors in reflexive ces_p give reverse bound against every compact operator. Integral test H_p(m+1)~m^(1−p)/(p−1) yields asymptotic and spectral radius. Independently checked 12 Hurwitz-ratio cases and the Tonelli identities for sample nonnegative vectors; analytical proof covers all m,p,b.

value.rationale: The exact operator/essential-norm gap and extremizer rigidity settle natural operator-geometric questions for a canonical homogeneous-tree model. In particular at critical b|λ|=1, essential norms remain 1 while usual power norms grow polynomially with sharp coefficient. This distinguishes spectral boundedness from norm dynamics in a natural infinite-dimensional setting.

final_claim: For full b-ary rooted tree b≥2, p>1 and constant λ≠0, norm of m-th Cesàro backward shift is (b|λ|)^m(ζ(p)/H_p(m+1))^(1/p), essential norm is (b|λ|)^m, with exactly common-phase inputs on level m as nonzero norm extremizers, asymptotic coefficient ((p−1)ζ(p))^(1/p) and both spectral radii b|λ|.
